overview: Hanna City is a planetary capital on Chandrila, documented across Films · Aftermath era · Mandalorian references. Hanna City on Chandrila hosted the New Republic Senate and Mon Mothma's post-Imperial reconstruction government.
history:
Hanna City began as a planetary capital anchor on Chandrila, positioned where water, ore, hyperspace lanes, or sacred geography forced travelers to stop. Hanna City grew where Chandrila's resources—water, ore, kyber, or trade lanes—forced travelers to stop, creating a planetary capital that outlasted first founders. Early survey maps from the Old Republic era list Hanna City as a mandatory customs point for sector governors and Jedi exploration teams. Films, Clone Wars, Rebels, Mandalorian, Ahsoka, KOTOR, KOTOR II, TOR, and Sith Empire narratives all treat Hanna City as more than scenery—it is a decision point.

Ancient and pre-Republic layers beneath Hanna City include buried fortresses, Rakatan relics, and Sith ward-stones that still disrupt modern sensors. Pre-Republic and Sith-era layers beneath Hanna City include ward-stones, Rakatan markers, and Massassi masonry that modern engineers still discover during repaving. High Republic pathfinders logged Hanna City as a waypoint during the Great Hyperspace Rush, leaving beacon towers that later wars repurposed as artillery spotters. Local archives recovered from Chandrila suggest Hanna City once governed trade policy for entire subsectors before centralization on Coruscant.

In the modern era, Hanna City expanded through prefab districts, orbital elevators, and refugee camps that fused multiple species into a single urban rhythm. Clone Wars, Imperial occupation, and New Republic rebuilding each added districts to Hanna City; Mandalorian and Ahsoka-era storylines treat it as a live operational hub. Mandalorian-era bounties and Ahsoka-era investigations repeatedly lead back to Hanna City because its ports lack the scrutiny of Core World bureaucracy. New Republic planners studied Hanna City as a template for rebuilding settlements after the Imperial collapse, citing both its failures and its innovations.

Hanna City has been invaded, liberated, blockaded, and rebuilt more times than most planetary capitals, making its streets a palimpsest of battle damage. Battle dossiers from KOTOR sieges, TOR planetary incursions, and Galactic Civil War raids mark Hanna City as strategically contested on Chandrila. Clone Wars dossiers mark Hanna City as strategically vital; Imperial Era governors exploited that same geography to punish rebellious populations. KOTOR-era records and TOR-era campaign logs show earlier iterations of the same struggle—control of Hanna City meant control of Chandrila.
significance:
The economy of Hanna City runs on layered industries: docking fees, black-market mediation, sacred tourism, factory output, or casino finance depending on the era. Hanna City's economy mixes legal trade with shadow finance—dock fees, kolto or tibanna exports, scavenging, or casino revenue depending on era and governor. Trade guilds from the Techno Union to the Mining Guild filed competing claims on Hanna City infrastructure during the late Republic. Post-war reconstruction funds often bypass Hanna City officially while flowing through its shadow banks—an open secret among Bothan analysts.

Cultural life in Hanna City mixes planetary tradition with imported habits from every species that ever missed a connection and stayed. Markets, cantinas, and temples in Hanna City blend Chandrila native ritual with offworld imports, producing music and cuisine that signal rebel safe houses to trained eyes. Music, food, and festival calendars in Hanna City are used by rebels to signal safe houses and by Imperials to track dissident networks. Jedi historians note that some of the galaxy's quietest acts of mercy—evacuations, forged transit papers, hidden healers—were organized in Hanna City back alleys.

Hanna City influences galactic history disproportionately because leaders, smugglers, and prophets treat it as neutral ground until it suddenly is not. Treaties, betrayals, and superweapon strikes linked to Hanna City altered fleet movements across the Old Republic through Sequel Era conflicts. Scenes set in Hanna City across the saga often mark turning points: treaties signed, betrayals exposed, or the first shot of a regional war. Settlement planners across the Rim still cite Hanna City when arguing for open ports versus fortified capitals—a debate renewed after every occupation.
